summary: Mephentermine is an indirectly acting sympathomimetic vasopressor used to prevent and treat hypotension, particularly that associated with spinal or epidural anaesthesia, and to support blood pressure in hypotensive/shock states. It acts mainly by releasing noradrenaline from sympathetic nerve endings, producing a positive inotropic effect and peripheral vasoconstriction with a relatively gradual and sustained rise in blood pressure; cardiac output is usually maintained or increased, and reflex bradycardia may occur. It is given intramuscularly or by slow intravenous injection (commonly 15-30 mg, repeated or by titrated infusion). Because it is not FDA-approved, dosing follows the British National Formulary, manufacturer information and established anaesthetic/Indian clinical practice. It should be used cautiously in hypertension, cardiovascular disease and hyperthyroidism, and is contraindicated with monoamine oxidase inhibitors and in phaeochromocytoma. Tachyphylaxis can develop with repeated dosing.

moa: Mephentermine is a sympathomimetic amine that acts mainly indirectly by displacing and releasing noradrenaline from postganglionic sympathetic nerve endings, with some weak direct alpha- and beta-adrenergic activity. The released noradrenaline stimulates beta-1 receptors in the heart (positive inotropic and chronotropic effects) and alpha receptors in the peripheral vasculature (vasoconstriction), raising blood pressure. Cardiac output is generally maintained or increased and the pressor effect has a relatively slow onset and prolonged duration; reflex vagal slowing of the heart may accompany the rise in blood pressure. Repeated dosing can deplete neuronal noradrenaline stores, leading to tachyphylaxis.

Known hypersensitivity to mephentermine or sympathomimetic amines

Chronic illness, concealed haemorrhage or hypovolaemia not yet corrected
Use with general anaesthetics that sensitise the myocardium (e.g. halothane/cyclopropane)

preg: Mephentermine is used in obstetric anaesthesia to treat maternal hypotension during spinal/epidural block. Vasopressors can affect uteroplacental perfusion, so use the lowest effective dose with continuous monitoring; weigh maternal benefit against fetal risk.
lact: Limited data are available on excretion in breast milk. Single peri-procedural doses are generally considered compatible with breastfeeding, but use with caution.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is established; titrate to blood-pressure response.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is established.

Beta-blockers - unopposed alpha effect/hypertension; blunted beta response

missed: Not applicable - mephentermine is an injectable vasopressor given by a healthcare professional during a procedure, not a self-administered scheduled medicine.
overdose: Overdose causes excessive sympathomimetic effects: marked hypertension, tachyarrhythmia or reflex bradycardia, anxiety, tremor, convulsions and, in severe cases, cerebral haemorrhage. There is no specific antidote. Stop the drug and manage supportively; severe hypertension may be treated with a short-acting alpha-blocker (e.g. phentolamine) or vasodilator, and arrhythmias with appropriate antiarrhythmic measures, under continuous monitoring.
